SMTO-EXE-0126 — SMTO can't tell whether the browser step happened

GUID: 0104da3a-e741-5b1f-b145-1643d9b4079b
Slug: browser-operation-outcome-unknown
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • SMTO sent a browser action, such as a click or form entry, but never got a clear answer back. The action may or may not have happened, so SMTO won't repeat it on its own.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Don't ask SMTO to repeat the step yet. Ask it to look at its browser and describe the page, without clicking anything. The page may already show the result, such as a confirmation message.
  2. Check the website or system directly, for example a confirmation email, order list or sent messages, to see whether the action went through. If SMTO's browser was lost, the website itself is the only reliable record.
  3. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and check the Gateway is connected. A dropped Gateway connection is a common reason SMTO never got an answer.
  4. Only if you are sure it did not happen, ask SMTO to do the step again and approve it when asked. Repeating an action that already happened could submit, send or buy something twice.

What success looks like

  • You've confirmed the action happened exactly once, or it has been done once after you confirmed it hadn't.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with what the step was meant to do, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't repeat the step until you've confirmed on the website that it didn't happen.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A browser write was dispatched, but its result was lost or incomplete (Gateway response lost, outer wait expired, or an error after the action began), so its effect is unknown.

What this means

  • A possible browser mutation lost its usable receipt or completion after dispatch, a pre-effect-looking exception followed an attempted action, or the outer service wait expired. The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.

Why this can happen

  • A possible browser mutation lost its usable receipt or completion after dispatch, a pre-effect-looking exception followed an attempted action, or the outer service wait expired.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original action, same-session page/snapshot/download evidence and any external outcome; do not replay merely to obtain a better receipt.

How to fix it

  • Produced by the browser skill when the Gateway call fails after dispatch with remote_effect_possible, by BrowserService.execute when the outer wait (MAX_TIMEOUT_MS + 5 s) expires, and by _execute when an error follows mark(). Do not replay the write. Inspect browser.page_info, browser.snapshot and browser.downloads, and verify the effect at the destination site, before authorizing a new action; sessions do not survive a Gateway restart.
  • Do not replay the mutation. Inspect browser.page_info, browser.snapshot and browser.downloads and reconcile the external effect first.

Retry and execution caution

  • Do not replay the mutation. Inspect browser.page_info, browser.snapshot and browser.downloads and reconcile the external effect first.

How to verify the fix

  • The original external effect is reconciled before another mutation is authorized.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, scan CDP endpoints, or export cookies/passwords/storage.

Technical notes

  • The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
